To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Oxytocinergic cells of the paraventicular hypothalamic nucleus are involved in food entrainment.

1) OTergic cells of PVN and supraoptic nucleus are activated by feeding, 2) a subset of OTergic cells in the dorsal and cau-dal part of PVN is active before the scheduled feeding time, 3) this activation persists in fasted rabbits at the scheduled feeding time.
the activation of the oxytocinergic system in the PVN is involved in the food entrainment mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how a food entrained activity rhythm is organized in the central nervous system, and the possible role of the OTergic cells in the caudal part PVN as an important component for food entrainment.
the role of the hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis in food anticipatory activity and its relationship to peripheral oscillators.
the study of the central organization of food entrainment in a natural model of this phenomenon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

food entrainment is a dynamic process that requires the participation of a complex system of central and periphery oscillators and that the PVN may play a main role as a central hub in the food entrainment system.
food entrainment involves the activation of OTergic cells of different PVN subdivisions, which may be involved in the central oscillation of the FAA.
food-entrained OTergic activity of the PVN may play a role in the expression of FAA and food synchronization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

OTergic cells in the PVN are involved in the central oscillator for FAA and that the dorsal and caulal part of the main PVN may play a role in the entrainment and synchronization of the peripheral oscillators for food entrainment.
food anticipatory activity is driven by a distributed network of central oscillators that are entrained by food cues and the hormone oxytocin is one of the main signals for this entrainment.
OT may be a synchronizing signal for food entrainment, and that a specific population of OTergic cells of PVN may play a role in the central clock mechanism that generates FAA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
food entrainment is a complex process that involves several brain areas, and the OTergic system of the PVN is an important component for this process.
OT is involved in food synchronization and that the OTergic cells of PVN are part of a central oscillatory mechanism that drives FAA.

OTergic cells in the PVN play a role in food entrainment, and the fact that they show a pattern of activation before the time for food suggests that they may participate in the central oscillation mechanism of FAA.
